title: The §6.4 ¶3 upload response, as the constructor for it builds one

source.note: composed: this is `Message::upload_response`'s output, for the URI recorded as this case's `expect.message.submessages[0].content`. A test in `crates/conformance/tests/` calls the constructor with that string and asserts it still produces exactly this file's `canonical_json`, so the shape is pinned from both ends. §6.4 ¶3 fixes the shape — "a message with MessageType field set to 'control' containing a submessage with the format field set of 'structured' and subformat of a URI" — so the URI is in a *submessage* and the first submessage stays the message's own text, which is the half a bare `structured`/`uri` message cannot supply.

input: {"messagetype":"control","format":"text","subformat":"english","content":"Send large binary content to the end-point named in the submessage below.","submessages":[{"format":"structured","subformat":"uri","content":"https://agent.example.com/nlip/upload/9f2"}]}

message.content: Send large binary content to the end-point named in the submessage below.

expect.text: Send large binary content to the end-point named in the submessage below.
expect.canonical_json: {"messagetype":"control","format":"text","subformat":"english","content":"Send large binary content to the end-point named in the submessage below.","submessages":[{"format":"structured","subformat":"uri","content":"https://agent.example.com/nlip/upload/9f2"}]}

notes: `ecma-430/27` records the same shape as a document a peer sent, with a sentence of its own for the first submessage; this one records what the constructor writes there, which is fixed and is part of what the test pins. The first submessage's text is not a rule of §6.4 — the clause says only that the response is a `control` message containing a `structured`/`uri` submessage — so an implementation whose own constructor writes a different sentence fails this case and breaks no clause. What it may not do is put the URI in the first submessage: §5.1.4 has already spoken for that one, and `/27`'s `notes` record the reading of "subformat of a URI" that leaves the URI a place to go.
